content: Herdr is a Rust agent multiplexer with a persistent server owning PTYs and one or more terminal clients. Visible model: workspace > tab > pane. Server exposes a local Unix socket (or Windows named pipe) with newline-delimited JSON RPC: session.snapshot, workspace.*, tab.*, pane.* (split, read, send_text, send_keys, resize, zoom), agent.*, layout.*, events.subscribe. No authentication token. For GUI terminal embedding, the documented surface is the CLI 'herdr terminal session control <pane|terminal|agent>' (writable, one controller, --takeover, --cols/--rows) emitting newline-delimited JSON 'terminal.frame' with base64 ANSI bytes plus 'terminal.closed'; stdin accepts terminal.input/resize/scroll/mouse/release (only mouse payload documented). 'terminal session observe' is read-only, multiple observers. Both were introduced in preview build 2026-06-30 and are documented in preview docs (build 2026-10-14), not explicitly stable. Full TUI attach ('herdr terminal attach', or bare herdr) requires a TTY. There is also an undocumented binary herdr-client.sock used by GUI projects; not public. No global terminal output event; events not replayed; no absolute PTY resize RPC except control --cols/--rows (respawn on host resize recommended). Herdr is AGPL-3.0-or-later or commercial.
